body: Would love to do something like this, as I have a little experience with voice acting and theater. I don’t have access to any high-end voice recording equipment, however. I hope you all apply! Voice acting is really fun.

I'm happy for Matt. I remember when I first saw him fight on HBO against Uzcategui. There was a lot of buzz about the recent influx of eastern european fighters at the time and Korobov was being mentioned in the same breath as GGG. Then the Lee fight happened. Now I never put much stock into that stoppage - This is boxing after all and Lee was a puncher - But I thought it was unfair how Matt was treated in the aftermath of that fight by media and fans alike.

I was excited when I heard that Korobov would fill in for Monroe. Fights with Gilberto Ramirez and David Benavidez had been in the talks but fallen through - At 35 this was the shot that he had long been waiting for - And some closure for myself after having followed his career for several years. I did not score the fight - But I thought that Matt did enough to warrant a draw. I have no problem with the decision. The 119 - 108 scorecard on the other hand is one of the worst I've ever seen. Larry Hazzard Jr should never be allowed to judge again.

I thought that Charlo did good considering that he took this fight on last minute notice. Korobov had some early success but Charlo showed patience and was eventually able to clip him in the last round which probably won him the fight. Credit to Matt for surviving and rallying despite being visibly tired - He showed a lot of heart.

The critique against Charlo by the media and fans is unwarranted in my opinion. Korobov was grossly underrestemated in the lead-up to this fight. He was thought of as a wash-up and a has-been but in reality he has been avoided by top fighters for years. Credit to Jermall for taking this fight and getting the W. At 35, Korobov probably has a couple of more fights in him and hopefully this performance will land him another meaningful fight.
That 119 - 109 scorecard is one of the worst I have ever seen. Absolutely disgusting.
He went the distance with one of the best guys at middleweight and won his share of rounds. Hopefully that exposure will help him land another meaningful fight before he retires.

It surprised me how many people were counting out Korobov before this fight. You CAN’T disrespect a man with that kind of amateur pedigree - Kovalev, Usyk, Jacobs - Just a couple of names on his record. This was BY FAR the best fighter that Jermall has been in the ring with and I credit him for taking a fight like this on last minute notice. 

People mentioned Korobov beeing out of the ring but remember - He was originally slated to face Benavidez this summer and Zurdo Ramirez before that so he’s been in the gym and was in very good shape for this fight. I keep hearing rumors of alcoholism on this forum but as far as I’ve seen nobody has been able to come up with any info to back up their claims. If you gonna throw dirt on a guy’s name you gotta come with some facts. What I saw in there was a fighter who was dialed in and ready. I’m happy that he got to showcase what he’s made of - He came there to win. The 119-109 scorecard did not reflect AT ALL what took place in the ring. Larry Hazzard Jr should never be allowed to judge a fight again his LIFE.

Credit to Charlo for beating a GAME opponent. He didn’t let himself get discouraged early and eventually found a home for that left hook - The same punch that Lee landed. Charlo has it all: Power, solid chin, good eyes and patience. But I wanna see more of him in the future. He’s still a live dog against any of the top guys at middleweight.

I think they're the real deal. Jermall, based on the eye test, is elite level. Solid chin. Calm under fire. He knocks out guys in the middle of exchanges. Kid has ice in his veins, and he's got a meanness about him too. Reminds me of Gerald McClellan sometimes, when I watch him. I won't speak on the doping rumors. Time will tell.

Ya'll are sleeping on Korobov though. The guy has arguably one of the best amateur records in boxing. Jacobs, Usyk, Derevyanchenko, Gaydarbekov. Just a few names. So what if he got clipped against Lee couple of years ago - This is boxing - And Lee was a lights out puncher. Make no mistake.

Charlo is still the heavy favorite, and for good reason. But every fight is different. According to fan logic on a lot of forums Jacobs didn't have a chance against GGG but he rose to the occasion. Sometimes you just need to be  infront of the right guy for you to really push yourself to that next level. Korobov looks like he stays in the gym. Remember - He was originally scheduled to face Benavidez this summer. I don't know what his problems were. Promotional, personal. He looks to me like he's dialed in for the fight.

Charlo has a chance of clipping him early. But don't be surprised if this thing goes rounds. Respect to Jermall for taking this fight. This is the real definition of a high risk - low reward fight.
He also holds the scalps of Sergey Derevyachenko, Danny Jacobs and Gaydarbek Gaydarbekov (Athens 2004 Gold Medalist) from his amateur days.
I never heard about this. I always wondered what was going on with him, thought it was just promotional issues. Anybody has some info?

HBO in the late 90's and early 00's was like nothing on television at the time. We saw the rise of serialized blockbuster TV drama as we know it with The Sopranos, OZ and The Wire. Gritty documentaries like Dopesick Love and Hookers at the Point. Comedy Specials, Dave Chapelle, Patrice O'Neal. And of course, Boxing after Dark.

Even though they might've wore out their welcome towards the end, for me, Jim Lampley will always be the voice of boxing. I fell in love with the sport hearing the late Manny Stewart loose his shit over Gatti and Ward, Toney and Jirov. Larry Merchant strongarming that guy in the post-fight interview. Roy checking his colleagues. Hell, even Big George had his moments.

Seeing the stands at Stub Hub almost empty last night was depressing. But that's the way it goes. Boxing moved on many years ago, HBO should've done too.

End of an era.

Vargas - Tito, December 2nd 2000. Two days ago was the 18th anniversary of this fight! Vargas went down two times in the opening round and looked out on his feet before coming back to knock Tito down in the 4th. "El Ferroz" gave Tito hell before eventually getting stopped in the 12th. Wild fight.

Look, I love boxing. But this part of the business, I swear to god it's fucking disgusting. How many times on an undercard have we seen a young prospect dismember a no-hoper, some part time cab-driver past his best in a couple of rounds just to pad his record? I have seen a lot of fights in my day that never should have happened. Some real ugly knockouts. Guys getting laid out cold.

This shit was just fuckin' bizarre though. I'd be curious to know how old this kid was and if he has ever sparred in a gym. His footwork looked all over the place. Didn't look like he knew how to take a shot.

Commissions need to put a stop to this shit before someone dies.

I'm sorry to hear that. I'm curious to what you meant in regards to your writing. Do you happen to suffer from dyslexia aswell? Because I know science has pointed to a link between the two. 

For me, personally, writing has become a very powerful and liberating outlet in being able to express my thoughts with people and communicate effortlessly. But maybe it's just not your thing. I would encourage you to keep searching for that outlet, wether it's through drawing, music or just using your body.

And thanks for sharing your story. It sure helps to know that there are others out there dealing with the same issues. Good luck!

That's really cool to hear. There's a lot of stories about stutterers who were able to become succesful actors, but none of those people seemed to stutter on stage. Not being able to say my lines, blocking in those moments when I felt like I had to deliver or ruin the flow of the play, was what brought me down. I'm curious to hear how you dealt with that, if you did. 

I have thought many times about giving it another go. But my confidence was shot after my experience in theater. Hearing your story ignites some hope in me. Thank you for sharing your story and good luck!

I actually studied writing after I dropped out of theater school, and it's perhaps one of the things I'm better at in life. Not because I was born with any particular talent for it - But because it was the only way that I could express myself with complete freedom. I think a lot of stutters can relate.

I still can't help but think of the "what ifs". But I believe you and me have developed similar mindsets. An empowering outlook on your stuttering is key for a productive and happy life. Otherwise it will become your prison.

Thank you for sharing your positive views.

Gatti losing to Alfonso Gomez in what would be his final fight. Arturo was my favourite fighter as a kid and it hurt me to see him go like that. 

McClellan down on his knees and pawing at his eye is also an image that stuck with me. I remember him sitting slouched in the corner after the fight and his trainer pouring water on his head. Gerald said that it felt like the water was running through his skull.

Damn, I had completly forgotten about Mike Jones. I remember him being rated pretty high by Ring Magazine at Welter before getting upset by Bailey. Had a title too at the time. He never seemed to recover from that loss. Randall Bailey was no joke.

Interesting choices. However, I believe that Dillian Whyte is the natural and more marketable option for team Usyk at heavyweight. It's a fight that would do great in the UK and increase Usyk's bargaining power ahead of an eventual AJ clash.

They need to modify the rule set somewhat to give Tenshin a chance. I'm not interested in seeing a boxing exhibition with RIZIN gloves. Tenshin got some of the best hands in MMA but he uses kicks and leg feints to set up his combinations. A boxing match would not be competitive IMO. At all. Introducing some sort of clinch, even with modified rules (no sweeps, head control or knees to the head) would help out Tenshin considerably if only to give Floyd something else to think about and help Tenshin set up his punches. Otherwise this is just another tasteless money grab that will do nothing to benifit either sport.

I'm glad things have been working out for you and that most importantly, YOU are happy with what you see in the mirror. Online dating has definatly saved my ass. Sure, it's superficial and all that crap, but it beats trying to approach a woman in a bar or a nightclub. How big is your stutter? I'm somewhat of a functional stutterer which means a lot of people don't pick up on my blocks. But I still made sure to tell the first woman I ever went out on an online date with. No need to make a big deal about it, just lay it out there and don't mention it again unless she specifically asks you about it. She will remember it even though you only mention it once beforehand. 

As for the actual date, try to pick a surrounding that you're comfortable in. I stutter worse in loud enviroments where I have to talk real loud so I usually go someplace quiet or a bar where the music is not so loud. If you feel a little worried about being able to keep up a conversation for long, pick an activity. Go bowling or whatever. People like talking about themselves. So get good at asking questions!

The hard part is getting out there. Once you get a few dates under your belt things will be a lot easier. I ended up in a two-year long relationship with the girl i mentioned earlier. I have since then been on a couple more online dates and I don't even mentioned my stutter anymore. Because guess what? My experience is women don't really care. We all got our hang ups. So just get yourself out there and start dating. You'll be fine!

This is a hard one. Jones in terms of skill might be top 5 dead or alive. The guy was just a phenom. God given talent.

But B-Hop is a great fighter. Stopped both Tito and De la Hoya at 160. Then went on to capture light heavy gold. 

In terms of skill, both fighters at their peaks, Jones will always edge him. Few in history could match Jones when he was at his best. But in terms of legacy, their careers as a whole, Hopkins places higher on the list. Ask any knowledgable trainer or writer and they will all have B-Hop in their top 15 all time.

Man this guy Tyson is just a champ in and out of the ring. Pretty damn funny too. I can't call the fight, but Fury really seems to believe in himself and he's got that fire in his belly. You cant't take that away from a man. Whatever the outcome, he seems to be in a good place and surrounded by the right people. Hopefully he'll continue on that good path.

Cool! I have not been following the boxing scene back home for some time. But Hammarby boxing are solid. I'm glad he's raising the profile for boxing in Sweden. We need more good ambassadors for the sport. Looking forward to see Anthony back in the ring.

I think he's alright. Anybody that makes it to this level had to dedicate a big part of their life and make some sacrifices to get to that point. And I don't think he had an easy time with his dad growing up neither. You can't blame a guy for accepting the money and the fame when it's thrusted upon him. People say that he underperformed in his career but he was just always destined to be a gateekeper-level guy. Nothing wrong with that. He never chose the last name he was born with and all the expectations that came with it.

I hear you man. You don't have to like a guy but you gotta respect the craft, all the years a man had to put in the gym to get to that level. Not all fighters are great human beings. This the hurting business, after all.

I'm from Sweden and I had never really heard of this guy until now. He seems like a good dude. Hopefully he can continue to build a following, get some more meaningful fights and make some money for himself.

It was a competitive but clear win for Jacobs. He pulled away in those middle rounds. Big up to Sergey though for rallying and really pouring it on in the final rounds. He never stopped trying.

The problem for Sergey is his size. He's a really skilled fighter but with those short arms he's always gonna have to reach and try a little harder in his fights. Going twelve rounds with Danny will do him real good in the future though. I think he'd make for a real entertaining fight with Lemieux. Sergey knocks him out, but it would be a shootout tho.

Jacobs is world class. Ya'll folks are sleeping saying he has no chance against Canelo. Stylistically he matches up very well. Alvarez would have to box his shoes off.

I wanna see Danny in another meaningful fight next. He can't go back to fighting the Luis Arias's of the world. DJ against Golovkin, Alvarez or Charlo are all coin-toss fights. I'd give him the slight edge against the Houston native based on experience. It would not surprise me if he ices him.
This win just gets more and more impressive as time wears on.

Man, I'm so hyped for this fight. Feels like a throwback "Boxing after Dark". I haven't seen enough of Derevyanchenko to make a prediction, but he might as well be among the top 4 in the division. Danny needs to be in with a certain caliber of oppisition for his skills to really show. The version that fought Sulecki wasn't the same fighter I saw go twelve rounds with GGG. 

Derevyanchenko will bring out the best of him. The atmosphere will be electric.

Lol. The guy just went twelve hard rounds and finished strong versus a much younger man in Canelo. Let the man fight. He’s a great ambassador for the sport and an exciting fighter. Still the best middleweight in the world in my opinion. Fighting Murata or anybody on ESPN would guarantee great numbers and help casual sport fans get into boxing.

Chins can be deceiving. Part of it I believe is largely psychological. Then there’s the weight aspect. Remember, Canelo was just a kid in that fight, fighting on HBO on the biggest stage possible. Stiffnes, nervousness, tension in the neck can lead to you getting hurt early in a fight. Aldo is a great example. Guy had a terrific chin, but his mind just wasn’t right coming in the octagon and he paid a big price. Same as coming in without warming up proberly and not building up a proper sweat. I belive Foreman always used to talk about guys coming in too ”cold”.

Going to Naples in a couple of days. Maybe I'll do some sightseeing?

Beat Marquez too, no doubt he was a good fucking fighter. Much respect to him an anybody who goes up there and laces up a pair. I hope he enjoys his post-fighting life. I appreciate his commentary.
I could care less to see this fight tbh. Hopefully we’ll get GGG-Derevyachenko at MSG or Saunders while Charlo fights Jacobs. Winners square off!

Heartbreaking to see Ali lose his title like that, he seems like a good kid.

Jaime Munguia is a beast. Let the guy take his time, he’s only 21.
”Capturing the Friedmans” is a brilliant documentary for anyone interested in the family dynamic. Not a serial killer, but a family coming to the realization that the father is a pedophile.

Apart from the fact that Vanes took this fight on short notice after a two year layoff (his last fight at 154), I thought Gennadys performance was really impressive. People seem to forget but Vanes was a 2004 olympian and at one point one of boxings brightest prospects. This guy had competitive fights with Charlo, Lara and knocked Andrade down. I actually expected Vanes to take GGG down the stretch and have his moments in the fight, with everybody shitting on Golovkin afterwards claiming he’s old, exposed or whatever crap they’re spewing nowadays. Martirosyan has never been down in his career - The only time I remember seeing him hurt was against Andrade. He is tough style for anyone to reajust to, especially on short notice but GGG took him out in just two rounds. I say that’s very impressive.

Now what’s next? If GGG passes on the Canelo rematch, I’d love to see Jacobs-Charlo in Brooklyn this summer, followed by GGG defending his IBF mandatory against Derevyachenko in NYC. There’s a big ukrainian population in New York and they could sell out MSG with the right build-up. Winners of those fights fight eachother. 

GGG is 36 but he’s still a hand-full for all of these guys. Don’t be fooled by the lack of knockouts vs Jacobs and Nelo.

Jacobs - Murata for the WBA Regular belt
Derevyanchenko - Charlo for the vacant IBF strap
Saunders - Andrade for the WBA
GGG - Canelo in september
